title: Perioperative management of anticoagulants and antiplatelets (elective surgery)
subject: anaesthesia
summary: Classify thrombotic and bleeding risk, stop warfarin 5 days before surgery, stop DOACs 1 to 2 days before by bleeding risk and renal function (longer for dabigatran with low CrCl), avoid heparin bridging except in the highest thrombotic risk, continue aspirin in most cases, and respect neuraxial intervals.

sections.title: Assess risk first
items: Record the drug, dose, indication, last dose, creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault), platelet count and any previous bleeding or thrombosis.

Classify procedural bleeding risk: minimal (most dental, skin, cataract, pacemaker implantation), low to moderate, or high (major abdominal, cancer, cardiac, intracranial, spinal, major orthopaedic, reconstructive or urological surgery, and any neuraxial block).

High thrombotic risk (bridging may be considered): mechanical mitral valve, older caged-ball or tilting-disc valve, stroke or TIA within the previous 3 to 6 months, VTE within 3 months or severe thrombophilia, rheumatic mitral valve disease with AF.
Urgent or emergency surgery on an anticoagulant is managed with reversal, not interruption (see the anticoagulant bleeding and reversal protocol).

sections.title: Warfarin and heparin bridging
items: Stop warfarin 5 days before surgery (CHEST: 5 to 7 days). Check INR the day before; if still above 1.5, many centres give low-dose oral vitamin K (1 to 2 mg).
Acenocoumarol (widely used in India) has a shorter half-life; still confirm a normal INR the day before surgery.
Resume warfarin at the usual dose on the evening of surgery or the next day (0 to 1 day after), once haemostasis is secure.

CHEST 2022 recommends against bridging in AF (strong), and suggests against bridging for VTE, for patients on DOACs, and even for most mechanical valves; reserve bridging for the highest-risk patients above after cardiology or haematology input.

If bridging: therapeutic LMWH (enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC 12-hourly) starting 3 days before surgery once INR falls; last dose about 24 hours before surgery (morning dose only the day before). IV UFH: stop 4 to 6 hours before.
Restart therapeutic LMWH about 24 hours after low or moderate bleed-risk surgery and 48 to 72 hours after high bleed-risk surgery; use prophylactic doses until then.

sections.title: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs)
items: Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban: omit for 1 day before low or moderate bleed-risk surgery (last dose 2 days before), and for 2 days before high bleed-risk surgery (last dose 3 days before).
Dabigatran, CrCl 50 mL/min or more: omit 1 day (low or moderate risk) or 2 days (high risk) before. CrCl 30 to 49 mL/min: omit 2 days or 4 days respectively.
No heparin bridging while a DOAC is interrupted, and no routine pre-operative DOAC level testing.
Resume the full DOAC dose about 24 hours after low or moderate bleed-risk surgery and 48 to 72 hours after high bleed-risk surgery; give prophylactic LMWH meanwhile if VTE risk is high.
Very low-risk procedures (for example some dental work, cataract, skin excision) can often proceed with minimal or no interruption; agree with the operator.

sections.title: Antiplatelet drugs
items: Aspirin: continue for most elective non-cardiac surgery (CHEST 2022 suggests continuation over interruption), and always around CABG. Stop only where bleeding would be catastrophic (for example some intracranial, spinal or posterior eye surgery), after discussion.
P2Y12 inhibitors, if stopping: clopidogrel 5 days, ticagrelor 3 to 5 days, prasugrel 7 days before surgery. Resume about 24 hours after surgery once haemostasis allows.

Recent coronary stent on dual antiplatelet therapy: defer elective surgery until the minimum dual therapy period is complete and plan jointly with cardiology; never stop aspirin in these patients without cardiology advice.
Pacemaker or ICD implantation on warfarin: continue warfarin (CHEST strong recommendation) rather than interrupting or bridging.

sections.title: Neuraxial and deep blocks (ASRA intervals)
items: LMWH: at least 12 hours after a prophylactic dose and 24 hours after a therapeutic dose before needle insertion or catheter removal (unchanged in ASRA 5th edition, 2025).

After neuraxial puncture: first prophylactic LMWH at least 12 hours later (therapeutic at least 24 hours), and at least 4 hours after catheter removal. Remove catheters before therapeutic LMWH is started.
SC UFH 5000 units 8 to 12-hourly: wait 4 to 6 hours after a dose (or check aPTT) before puncture or catheter removal. IV heparin: stop 4 to 6 hours before and confirm normal aPTT.
Warfarin: stopped 5 days with a normal INR; remove catheters when INR is below 1.5.

DOACs (ASRA 4th edition, 2018): rivaroxaban, apixaban and edoxaban 72 hours; dabigatran 120 hours. Restart no sooner than 6 hours after catheter removal. The 2025 edition also allows drug-level-guided decisions; follow local policy.
Clopidogrel and ticagrelor 5 to 7 days, prasugrel 7 to 10 days before neuraxial block. Aspirin or NSAIDs alone do not require interruption.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Routine bridging for AF or DOACs: increases major bleeding without reducing thromboembolism.
Using the same DOAC stop time for everyone: dabigatran with CrCl under 50 mL/min needs much longer.
Restarting full-dose anticoagulation too early after high bleed-risk surgery.
Stopping aspirin or both antiplatelets in a patient with a recent coronary stent.
Forgetting to plan neuraxial catheter removal around the timing of post-operative LMWH or DOAC doses.

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.dose: Stop 5 days before surgery; restart usual dose evening of surgery or next day
drugs.notes: Check INR day before; low-dose oral vitamin K if INR above 1.5 per local protocol.

drugs.name: Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban
drugs.dose: Omit 1 day (low or moderate bleed risk) or 2 days (high bleed risk) before surgery
drugs.notes: Resume 24 hours (low or moderate) or 48 to 72 hours (high) after. Neuraxial: 72 hours (ASRA).

drugs.name: Dabigatran
drugs.dose: CrCl 50 mL/min or more: omit 1 or 2 days. CrCl 30 to 49: omit 2 or 4 days (low-moderate vs high bleed risk)

drugs.name: Enoxaparin (bridging, therapeutic)
drugs.dose: 1 mg/kg SC every 12 hours; last dose about 24 hours before surgery
drugs.notes: Only for highest thrombotic risk; reduce to 1 mg/kg once daily if CrCl below 30 mL/min.

drugs.name: Unfractionated heparin (IV)
drugs.notes: Useful bridging agent in severe renal impairment.

drugs.name: Clopidogrel / ticagrelor / prasugrel
drugs.dose: Stop 5 / 3 to 5 / 7 days before surgery respectively
drugs.notes: Neuraxial: clopidogrel and ticagrelor 5 to 7 days, prasugrel 7 to 10 days.

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.dose: Continue 75 to 150 mg once daily through most surgery
drugs.notes: Stop only for closed-space surgery after discussion.
